en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll learn the words for your career and your education: applying for jobs, school and university, and your skills and experience. We'll also fix three mistakes that many Indonesians make on their CVs.

steps.title: Applying for a job
steps.text: Let's start with the job hunt, from the vacancy to the interview.
steps.body:
You **apply for** a job (melamar). Indonesian *melamar pekerjaan* has no little word in the middle, so learners write `apply a job`: English needs **for** before the thing you want (a job, a position, a scholarship). The company takes **to**: *apply to five companies*.

First you find a **vacancy** (US also **job opening**). You send your **CV** (British) or **résumé** (American, 'REZ-oo-may') with a **cover letter**. Then comes the **job interview**, and maybe they **hire** you.

pairs.id: lulusan baru (native speakers often say recent graduate)

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Sari saw a great vacancy on LinkedIn. Today she's writing her cover letter.

question.prompt: Complete: Sari is going to ___ the marketing job at a start-up in Jakarta.
question.explanation: The thing you want comes after **apply for**: *apply for a job*. `apply the job` copies Indonesian *melamar pekerjaan* with no little word, and *apply in* isn't used with a job.

steps.title: Life at work
steps.text: You got the job! Here are the words for working life.
steps.body:
Your **salary** is your monthly pay (gaji). A **full-time** job is about 40 hours a week; a **part-time** job is fewer hours. An **internship** is magang, and the person is an **intern**.

Work well and you **get a promotion** (naik jabatan). To leave, you **resign** (formal) or **quit** (relaxed). Trap: *resign* is only a verb, so Indonesian *surat resign* is a **resignation letter**.

If the company ends your job, you **lose your job**. Learn **get fired** (dipecat) and **get laid off** (kena PHK) as phrases.

steps.title: School and university in English
steps.text: Foreigners don't know SD, SMA or S1, so let's give them English names.
steps.body:
- SD = **primary school** (American: **elementary school**)
- SMP = **junior high school**, SMA = **senior high school**, SMK = **vocational high school**
- S1 = a **bachelor's degree**, S2 = a **master's degree**, S3 = a **PhD**

Your jurusan is your **major** (American): *My major is law.* British English says *I studied law*. A **scholarship** is beasiswa (like LPDP), and **tuition fees** are biaya kuliah (UKT). Recap from A2: skripsi is your **thesis**.

steps.title: lulus: pass or graduate?
steps.text: One Indonesian word, two English words. Watch the trap.
steps.body: You **pass** an exam or a test (lulus ujian). You **graduate from** a school or university (lulus sekolah/kuliah: you finish it). So `I passed from UI` is wrong. **A graduate** is a person (lulusan), and **graduation** is wisuda. Say the verb 'GRAJ-u-eit' and the noun 'GRAJ-u-et'.

examples.en: I passed the TOEFL test last month.
examples.id: Saya lulus tes TOEFL bulan lalu.

examples.en: Budi graduated from senior high school last year.
Rina is a fresh graduate from ITB.
My cousin majored in English at a university in Malang.
examples.id: Sepupu saya kuliah jurusan bahasa Inggris di sebuah universitas di Malang.

examples.en: My parents came to my graduation in Yogyakarta.
examples.id: Orang tua saya datang ke wisuda saya di Yogyakarta.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: It's the end of the semester. Sari's final exams were last week, and the results are out.

question.prompt: Complete: Good news! Sari ___ all her exams, so she can graduate in August.
question.explanation: *Lulus ujian* is **pass** an exam: *passed all her exams*. **graduate (from)** is for finishing a whole school or university, which Sari does later, in August.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Big news from Rina: she's going to study abroad, and she doesn't have to pay anything.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Rina mendapat beasiswa untuk kuliah di Jepang.
question.solution: Rina got a scholarship to study in Japan.
question.explanation: Beasiswa is **a scholarship** (one scholarship, so *a*). The reason comes after it with **to** + verb: *to study in Japan*.

steps.title: Skills and experience
steps.text: Last group: how to describe what you can do, on your CV or in an interview.
steps.body:
**experience** (pengalaman kerja) is uncountable: no *a*, no *-s*. Say **a lot of experience**, **two years of experience**, **work experience**; `many experiences` is wrong for work. (*An experience* is one event: *Bali was a great experience.*)

**skills** can be counted: *computer skills*. **Soft skills** are people skills; *hard skills* are usually **technical skills**.

You're **good at** something (not `good in`): *good at design, good at numbers*. You're **fluent in** a language. A **certificate** can make you **qualified for** a job.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Rina worked in a call centre from 2021 to 2024. Now she's writing her CV.

question.prompt: Which sentence is correct for her CV?
options: I have many experiences in customer service.
I have three years experiences in customer service.
I have three years of experience in customer service.
question.explanation: Work experience is uncountable: no *-s*, and not *many*. Count the years instead: **three years of experience**.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: In Dimas's office, everyone asks him for help with spreadsheets.

question.prompt: Complete: Dimas is very good ___ Excel.
question.explanation: The partner of *good* for a skill is **at**: *good at Excel* (jago Excel). `good in` copies Indonesian *pintar di*.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's the whole lesson on one page. Keep it for your next job application.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · Careers & education
artifact.intro: The key words for jobs, school and university, and skills, with the Indonesian traps.
rows: apply for a job (apply to a company)
a vacancy / a job opening; We're hiring!
a CV (UK) / a résumé (US), a cover letter
get a promotion; resign / quit, a resignation letter
naik jabatan; mengundurkan diri, surat pengunduran diri
lose your job, get fired, get laid off
primary (US: elementary), junior high, senior high, vocational high school
a bachelor's, a master's, a PhD
a major (US), a scholarship, tuition fees, a thesis
pass an exam / graduate from university, a graduate, graduation
lulus ujian / lulus kuliah, lulusan, wisuda
a lot of work experience, skills, a certificate
good at, fluent in, qualified for
tips: **apply for** the job you want, **apply to** the company: never `apply a job`.
**experience** at work has no -s: **a lot of experience**, not `many experiences`. And **good at**, not `good in`.
**lulus** = **pass** (an exam) or **graduate from** (a school or university).

examples.en: I'm going to apply for a job as a data analyst.
examples.id: Saya mau melamar pekerjaan sebagai analis data.

examples.en: She works part-time and gets a small salary.
examples.id: Dia kerja paruh waktu dan dapat gaji kecil.

examples.en: Dimas has a bachelor's degree in computer science.
I have a lot of experience in marketing, and I'm fluent in English.
examples.id: Saya punya banyak pengalaman di bidang pemasaran, dan saya fasih berbahasa Inggris.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kamu belajar kosakata untuk karier dan pendidikanmu: melamar pekerjaan, sekolah dan kuliah, serta kemampuan dan pengalamanmu. Kita juga akan membetulkan tiga kesalahan yang sering muncul di CV orang Indonesia.

steps.title: Melamar pekerjaan
steps.text: Kita mulai dari mencari kerja, dari lowongan sampai wawancara.
steps.body:
Melamar pekerjaan = **apply for** a job. *Melamar pekerjaan* tidak punya kata kecil di tengahnya, jadi banyak yang menulis `apply a job`: bahasa Inggris perlu **for** sebelum hal yang kamu inginkan (pekerjaan, posisi, beasiswa). Perusahaannya memakai **to**: *apply to five companies*.

Pertama kamu menemukan **vacancy** (lowongan; Amerika juga **job opening**). Kamu kirim **CV** (British) atau **résumé** (Amerika, 'REZ-u-mei') dengan **cover letter** (surat lamaran). Lalu ada **job interview**, dan semoga mereka **hire** you (menerimamu).

pairs.id: lulusan baru (penutur asli sering bilang recent graduate)

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Sari melihat lowongan bagus di LinkedIn. Hari ini dia menulis surat lamarannya.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Sari is going to ___ the marketing job at a start-up in Jakarta.
question.explanation: Hal yang kamu inginkan datang setelah **apply for**: *apply for a job*. `apply the job` meniru *melamar pekerjaan* tanpa kata kecil, dan *apply in* tidak dipakai dengan pekerjaan.

steps.title: Kehidupan kerja
steps.text: Kamu diterima! Ini kosakata untuk kehidupan kerja.
steps.body:
**salary** adalah gaji bulananmu. Kerja **full-time** sekitar 40 jam seminggu; kerja **part-time** lebih sedikit jamnya. **internship** adalah magang, dan orangnya disebut **intern**.

Kerja dengan baik dan kamu **get a promotion** (naik jabatan). Untuk keluar, kamu **resign** (resmi) atau **quit** (santai). Jebakan: *resign* hanya kata kerja, jadi *surat resign* adalah **resignation letter**.

Kalau perusahaan mengakhiri pekerjaanmu, kamu **lose your job**. Hafalkan **get fired** (dipecat) dan **get laid off** (kena PHK) sebagai frasa.

steps.title: Sekolah dan kuliah dalam bahasa Inggris
steps.text: Orang asing tidak tahu SD, SMA atau S1, jadi ayo pakai nama bahasa Inggrisnya.
steps.body:
- SD = **primary school** (Amerika: **elementary school**)
- SMP = **junior high school**, SMA = **senior high school**, SMK = **vocational high school**
- S1 = **bachelor's degree**, S2 = **master's degree**, S3 = **PhD**

Jurusanmu disebut **major** (Amerika): *My major is law.* Bahasa Inggris British bilang *I studied law*. **Scholarship** adalah beasiswa (seperti LPDP), dan **tuition fees** adalah biaya kuliah (UKT). Ingat dari A2: skripsi adalah **thesis**.

steps.title: lulus: pass atau graduate?
steps.text: Satu kata Indonesia, dua kata Inggris. Awas jebakannya.
steps.body: Kamu **pass** ujian atau tes (lulus ujian). Kamu **graduate from** sekolah atau universitas (lulus sekolah/kuliah: kamu menyelesaikannya). Jadi `I passed from UI` salah. **A graduate** adalah orangnya (lulusan), dan **graduation** adalah wisuda. Kata kerjanya dibaca 'GRAJ-u-eit', kata bendanya 'GRAJ-u-et'.

examples.en: I passed the TOEFL test last month.
examples.id: Saya lulus tes TOEFL bulan lalu.

examples.en: Budi graduated from senior high school last year.
Rina is a fresh graduate from ITB.
My cousin majored in English at a university in Malang.
examples.id: Sepupu saya kuliah jurusan bahasa Inggris di sebuah universitas di Malang.

examples.en: My parents came to my graduation in Yogyakarta.
examples.id: Orang tua saya datang ke wisuda saya di Yogyakarta.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Akhir semester. Ujian akhir Sari minggu lalu, dan hasilnya sudah keluar.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Good news! Sari ___ all her exams, so she can graduate in August.
question.explanation: *Lulus ujian* adalah **pass** an exam: *passed all her exams*. **graduate (from)** untuk menyelesaikan seluruh sekolah atau kuliah, dan itu baru terjadi nanti, bulan Agustus.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Kabar besar dari Rina: dia akan kuliah di luar negeri, dan dia tidak perlu bayar apa-apa.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Rina mendapat beasiswa untuk kuliah di Jepang.
question.solution: Rina got a scholarship to study in Japan.
question.explanation: Beasiswa adalah **a scholarship** (satu beasiswa, jadi pakai *a*). Tujuannya datang sesudahnya dengan **to** + kata kerja: *to study in Japan*.

steps.title: Kemampuan dan pengalaman
steps.text: Kelompok terakhir: cara menjelaskan kemampuanmu, di CV atau saat wawancara.
steps.body:
**experience** (pengalaman kerja) tidak dihitung satu per satu: tanpa *a*, tanpa *-s*. Bilang **a lot of experience**, **two years of experience**, **work experience**; `many experiences` salah untuk pengalaman kerja. (*An experience* adalah satu kejadian: *Bali was a great experience.*)

**skills** bisa dihitung: *computer skills*. **Soft skills** = kemampuan bergaul dan bekerja sama; *hard skills* biasanya disebut **technical skills**.

Kamu **good at** sesuatu (bukan `good in`): *good at design, good at numbers*. Kamu **fluent in** sebuah bahasa (fasih). **Certificate** (sertifikat) bisa membuatmu **qualified for** sebuah pekerjaan.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Rina bekerja di call centre dari 2021 sampai 2024. Sekarang dia menulis CV-nya.

question.prompt: Kalimat mana yang benar untuk CV-nya?
options: I have many experiences in customer service.
I have three years experiences in customer service.
I have three years of experience in customer service.
question.explanation: Pengalaman kerja (experience) tidak dihitung satu per satu: tanpa *-s*, dan bukan *many*. Hitung tahunnya saja: **three years of experience**.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Di kantor Dimas, semua orang minta bantuannya soal spreadsheet.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Dimas is very good ___ Excel.
question.explanation: Pasangan *good* untuk sebuah keahlian adalah **at**: *good at Excel* (jago Excel). `good in` meniru *pintar di* dalam bahasa Indonesia.
